entities.summary: Guy de Bourgogne, O.Cist., was a French monk, Abbot, and Cardinal of the Roman Catholic Church. Born of unknown origin, he rose to prominence in the 13th century as a leading figure in the Cistercian Order. In 1245, he became the Abbot of Cîteaux, where he oversaw the construction of numerous monasteries and abbeys across Europe. De Bourgogne's diplomatic skills and influence led to his appointment as Cardinal-Bishop of Ostia in 1252, making him a key advisor to Pope Innocent IV. He played a significant role in the Fourth Crusade, participating in the sack of Constantinople in 1204. De Bourgogne's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he helped shape the Cistercian Order into a powerful force in medieval Europe. His influence can be seen in the numerous monasteries and abbeys he founded, which became centers of learning, art, and spirituality. De Bourgogne's life serves as a testament to the enduring power of faith and the importance of leadership in shaping the course of history.
